kill_argument: The strongest remaining objection is dependence on an existing local software environment: matching installed metadata and a passing dependency check do not establish that a fresh machine can rebuild these unusually recent pins, including a development release of wrapt. That is a replication obligation, not evidence of a present code defect. I attacked the interpreter mismatch, missing transitive pins, conflicting execution order and undocumented changes to the estimator. The corrected manifest specifies Python 3.14, all thirteen installed distribution versions match the pins and recorded requirements hash, and pip check passes. The executable hashes are unchanged from round 1; spot-checks of the ATT, bootstrap, Holm and failure handling reveal no new divergence from the approved conditional design. C1 is resolved in the files. I ran only dependency metadata and import checks, never a model, estimate or study-data calculation. The eventual synthetic causal interpretation still depends on exchangeability, overlap and regular IID inference; software completion cannot establish those assumptions.
